title: Moss - Quill acknowledges the player
summary: A face becomes a relationship when its look and gestures answer the person in front of it.

observations.text: Lico describes deliberate eye contact, returning the player's wave, petting and high-five interactions as ways to build mutual acknowledgement and trust.
He requires personality to survive gameplay actions while input stays immediate and movement fluid; he explicitly seeks nuanced, honest gestures.
The GDC slides identify a reaction system, limited gameplay interruptions using idle cycles, and particle physics to help overlapping action.

mistIdeas: Our inference: give MIST a listening look that locks onto the user before a reply, then a small acknowledgement after understanding.
Our inference: prioritize an incoming user event over decorative idle motion, preserving the current facial pose into the response.
Our inference: let a secondary antenna or chassis settle finish after the principal eye reaction; never require that settle before accepting another event.

title: Dory prototype - independent eye and mouth controls

people.name: Chris (twocentstudios)
people.role: Solo developer and author of the Dory character prototype

summary: A small, unusually explicit prototype shows how graphic facial shapes can remain independent of body animation.

observations.text: The author models separate open and closed eye objects, parents them to the character's armature, and tests blink control with the action button.
He proposes named expressions pairing eye and mouth shapes, driven from dialogue; his working blink demo uses a separate Godot AnimationPlayer so body animation can continue.

mistIdeas: Our inference: keep expression choice, gaze, blink and speech-mouth controllers separate, with clear priorities when they overlap.
Our inference: prototype an emotional pose using a small set of deliberate shapes before adding continuous morphs. Independence should permit a listening mouth to remain still while the eyes react.

title: Farewell North - making the human companion responsive

people.name: Kyle Banks
people.role: Developer and author of the facial-animation devlog

summary: A solo developer documents the difficult jump from a face that merely exists to a character who can carry close dialogue.

observations.text: Banks reports that his human protagonist initially had to be kept distant or off-screen. His devlog describes adding eye tracking, blinking, expressions and lip sync with Unity, Blender and FaceIt.
He warns in his own description that expressions can quickly feel wrong and still require refinement; hiring animators and adding believable behaviour alone had not resolved the lifeless face.

mistIdeas: Our inference: review MIST at its actual conversation size, because a small distant character can conceal a weak face.
Our inference: evaluate gaze, blink, expression and speech as separate contributions; freeze three channels while judging the fourth, then restore them together.
